label: prop:hadron-q-self-correction
title: Effective substrate parameter: hadron self-deformation of $q$
html:
The substrate parameter q \colon M \to k^\times (substrate parameter) is a field, not a background constant. A hadron (hadron) is a multi-component knot composite containing internal Hopf junctions and crossings. It perturbs the local value of q through its topological linking structure. The effective substrate parameter observed by a nucleus is

  q_{\mathrm{eff}}(p, n)
  = 
  q_0 +  \delta q(p, n),

with background value q_0 (local substrate q) and hadron self-deformation \delta q(p, n).

Proposition. Let \mathcal{N}(Z, N) = Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n} be a nucleus (stable nucleus). The signed crossing excess—the imbalance between positive (\mathfrak{p}--\mathfrak{p}) and negative (\mathfrak{n}--\mathfrak{n}) Hopf crossings—determines the self-deformation of the substrate parameter:

  \delta q(p, n)
  = 
  \frac{\ell_{\mathrm{net}}(p, n)}{A^2}
  \cdot \hbar_q^2,
  \qquad
  \ell_{\mathrm{net}}(p, n)
  = 
  \binom{p}{2} - \binom{n}{2}
  = 
  \frac{p(p-1) - n(n-1)}{2},

where \hbar_q = 1 - q_0^{-1} is the quantum Planck constant. For neutron-rich nuclei (n > p), \ell_{\mathrm{net}} < 0 and the local q drops; for proton-rich nuclei, \ell_{\mathrm{net}} > 0 and q rises.
